title: Understand computer vision at work · Level 1
slo: Identify what computer vision does and match it to common workplace uses.

exercises.question_text: Which tasks are part of medical imaging analysis? Select all that apply.

options.text: Analyze X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans
options.rationale: This is correct. These scan types are used in medical imaging analysis.
This is correct. Such anomalies can be highlighted for review.
This is incorrect. Misplaced shelf products belong to retail monitoring.
options.better_fit: Retail shelf monitoring fits store inventory checks.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Lane recognition is a road-navigation use.
options.better_fit: Autonomous vehicle vision fits interpreting road markings.

exercises.explanation: Correct—medical imaging analysis assists with scan review and anomaly highlighting.

exercises.question_text: What can retail shelf monitoring detect?

options.rationale: This is correct. Cameras can detect missing or incorrectly placed shelf products.
This is incorrect. These are possible medical-image anomalies.
options.better_fit: Medical imaging analysis fits X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Factory product defects are a manufacturing use.
options.better_fit: Manufacturing defect detection fits assembly-line quality checks.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Lane markings are navigation information.
options.better_fit: Autonomous vehicle vision fits recognizing road features.

exercises.explanation: Correct—retail shelf monitoring checks availability and placement.

exercises.question_text: Computer vision can highlight possible anomalies, such as tumors or fractures, in medical images.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Potential anomalies could receive less attention.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Vision systems can highlight possible tumors or fractures in medical images.

exercises.explanation: Correct—this can assist radiologists reviewing scans.

exercises.question_text: Retail shelf monitoring helps radiologists find possible fractures in CT scans.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A store task would be confused with a radiology task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Retail shelf monitoring detects out-of-stock or misplaced store products.

exercises.question_text: What does computer vision help machines understand?

options.text: Visual information from images and video
options.rationale: This is correct. Computer vision interprets images, video, and camera feeds.
This is incorrect. Spoken audio is not visual input.
options.better_fit: Audio analysis fits tasks based on speech or sound recordings.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Creating an image differs from interpreting one.
options.better_fit: Image generation fits creating visuals from written prompts.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Spreadsheets do not supply visual scene information.
options.better_fit: Tabular-data analysis fits structured numerical records.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe object detection or image segmentation? Select all that apply.

options.text: Object detection finds objects and their locations
options.rationale: This is correct. Detection identifies presence and location.

options.text: Segmentation divides an image into meaningful regions
options.rationale: This is correct. Segmentation separates meaningful image areas.

options.text: Object detection creates an image from text
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Detection analyzes an existing image rather than generating one.
options.better_fit: Image generation fits creating a visual from text.

options.text: Segmentation converts spoken language into text
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Segmentation is an image-analysis process.
options.better_fit: Speech recognition fits transcribing spoken language.

exercises.explanation: Correct—detection locates objects, while segmentation divides image areas.

exercises.question_text: Computer vision only works with text and cannot interpret images or video.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Computer vision works with images, video, and live camera feeds.

exercises.question_text: Object detection identifies the presence and location of objects in an image or video.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Object positions would not be identified.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Object detection tells both that an object is present and where it appears.

exercises.explanation: Correct—location is a key part of object detection.

exercises.question_text: What can autonomous vehicles recognize with computer vision? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Road signs are visual information used for navigation.
This is correct. Recognizing pedestrians supports safe navigation.
This is correct. Lane markings support road-position decisions.
This is incorrect. Surface-defect inspection is a manufacturing use.
options.better_fit: Manufacturing defect detection fits assembly-line product inspection.

exercises.explanation: Correct—vehicles recognize road information and people to navigate safely.

exercises.question_text: Which workplace use checks assembly-line products for missing components?

options.rationale: This is correct. It inspects products for defects, misalignments, and missing components.
This is incorrect. It supports review of patient scans.
options.better_fit: Medical imaging analysis fits X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. It checks store inventory and placement.
options.better_fit: Retail shelf monitoring fits out-of-stock or misplaced products.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. It supports navigation in road environments.
options.better_fit: Autonomous vehicle vision fits recognizing road users and signs.

exercises.explanation: Correct—this is a manufacturing quality-control task.

exercises.question_text: Recognizing road signs, lane markings, pedestrians, and other vehicles supports safe navigation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A vehicle could navigate with less critical road information.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Recognizing signs, lanes, pedestrians, and vehicles supports safe navigation.

exercises.explanation: Correct—these visual details support informed road decisions.

exercises.question_text: Manufacturing defect detection uses cameras to find products that are out of stock or misplaced.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Factory inspection would be confused with store inventory.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Manufacturing defect detection finds product defects, misalignments, and missing components.

flashcards.back: AI that interprets visual information such as images, video, and camera feeds.
It identifies objects and their locations in images or video.
It divides an image into meaningful regions or object areas.
Detect out-of-stock or misplaced products using cameras.
